_comment: IFRC hazard codebook (2021) used as a CLUSTERING METHOD, not a list to render. Categories and definitions are the codebook's; membership comes from the data. hip_codes is keyed on the UNDRR-ISC HIP code and NOT on the nat-*-*-* slug: the slug is absent on ~38% of Montandon items, MH0103 and MH0301 share one, and where it is present it disagrees with the codebook twice - wildfire (UNDRR climatological, codebook non-technological) and extreme heat (UNDRR meteorological, codebook climatological). Definitions are the codebook's defining sentence, quoted exactly; the full paragraphs are on pages 7-9 of https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2021-06/04-HAZARD-DEFINITIONS-HR.pdf

detection_rules._comment: A 'detection' is a machine observation with no evidence of consequence. Only GDACS is configured, because only GDACS produces the problem: 385 of the first 500 region-wide events are its satellite fire detections, Green with zero people potentially affected. PDC and IDMC-IDU have no rule, so everything they publish is an 'event'.

categories.label: Climatological hazards
categories.definition: Hazards arising from long-lived, meso- to macro-scale atmospheric processes, from intra-seasonal to multi-decadal climate variability.

sub_hazards.label: Drought
sub_hazards.definition: A long-lasting event triggered by a lack of precipitation.

sub_hazards.label: Extreme heat / heat wave
sub_hazards.definition: A period during which the daily maximum temperature exceeds for more than five consecutive days the maximum normal temperature by 5 degrees Celsius.

sub_hazards.label: Extreme cold / cold wave
sub_hazards.definition: Marked cooling of the air, or the invasion of very cold air, over a large area.

sub_hazards.label: Extreme heat / drought (reported)
sub_hazards.definition: Document reporting of drought, extreme heat or water scarcity. One tag spanning two codebook hazards; splitting it would mean re-parsing the corpus.

categories.label: Biological hazards
categories.definition: Hazards of organic origin or conveyed by biological vectors, including exposure to pathogenic micro-organisms, toxins and bioactive substances.

sub_hazards.label: Biological emergency
sub_hazards.definition: A biological emergency can occur when there is a major epidemic outbreak of diseases, plant or animal contagion, insect or other animal plagues and infestations.

sub_hazards.label: Major epidemic and potential pandemic diseases
sub_hazards.definition: Either an unusual increase in the number of cases of an infectious disease that already exists in the region or population concerned, or the appearance of an infection disease previously absent from a region.

sub_hazards.label: Disease outbreak (reported)
sub_hazards.definition: Document reporting of cholera, measles, dengue, malaria, hepatitis or another epidemic.

categories.label: Geophysical hazards
categories.definition: Hazards originating from internal earth processes.

sub_hazards.label: Earthquake
sub_hazards.definition: A term used to describe both sudden slip on a fault, and the resulting ground shaking and radiated seismic energy caused by the slip, or by volcanic or magmatic activity, or other sudden stress changes in the earth.

sub_hazards.label: Landslide / debris flow
sub_hazards.definition: Movement of surface material down a slope.

sub_hazards.label: Tsunami
sub_hazards.definition: A sea wave of local or distant origin that results from large-scale seafloor displacements associated with strong earthquakes, major submarine slides, or exploding volcanic islands.

sub_hazards.label: Volcanic eruption
sub_hazards.definition: The discharge (aerially explosive) of fragmentary ejecta, lava and gases from a volcanic vent.

categories.label: Meteorological hazards
categories.definition: Hazards caused by short-lived, micro- to meso-scale extreme weather and atmospheric conditions that last from minutes to days.

sub_hazards.label: Tropical cyclone
sub_hazards.definition: An atmospheric closed low pressure circulation system rotating counter-clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.

sub_hazards.label: Thunderstorm / lightning
sub_hazards.definition: Convective storm with thunder and lightning. Not named in the codebook; placed here by the Meteorological definition above.

sub_hazards.label: Storm (violent wind)
sub_hazards.definition: Wind- and pressure-related convective storm, including dust and sand storms. Not named in the codebook; placed here by the Meteorological definition above.

categories.label: Hydrological hazards
categories.definition: Hazards caused by the occurrence, movement and distribution of surface and subsurface freshwater and saltwater.

sub_hazards.label: Floods
sub_hazards.definition: The overflowing of the normal confines of a stream or other body of water, or the accumulation of water over areas that are not normally submerged. This includes: river/fluvial floods.

sub_hazards.label: Storm surge
sub_hazards.definition: The temporary increase, at a particular locality, in the height of the sea due to extreme meteorological conditions.

sub_hazards.label: Hailstorms
sub_hazards.definition: Storms that produce hail that reaches the ground are known as hailstorms.

sub_hazards.label: Flooding (reported)
sub_hazards.definition: Document reporting of flood, heavy rain or inundation.

categories.label: Technological and man-made hazards
categories.definition: Hazards that are induced entirely or predominantly by human activities and choices. This term does not include the occurrence or risk of armed conflicts and other situations of social instability or tension that are subject to international humanitarian law and national legislation.

sub_hazards.label: Man-made hazards
sub_hazards.definition: Hazards that are induced entirely or predominantly by human activities and choices.

sub_hazards.label: Nuclear emergency
sub_hazards.definition: Nuclear emergencies involve or emerge from nuclear chain reactions.

sub_hazards.label: Radiological emergency
sub_hazards.definition: Radiological emergencies can involve all other sources of radiation, such as radiography machines, radioactive material for use in industry, lost sources and more.

sub_hazards.label: Chemical emergency
sub_hazards.definition: Any unplanned event involving hazardous substances that causes or is liable to cause harm to health, the environment or property.

categories.label: Non-technological and man-made hazards
categories.definition: Man-made hazards outside the technological group.

sub_hazards.label: Wildfires
sub_hazards.definition: This includes all types of fire events, wildfires and forest fires. It is the process of combustion of inflammable materials producing heat, flames and (often) smoke.

categories.label: Conflict and violence
categories.definition: NOT an IFRC codebook category. The codebook explicitly excludes armed conflict from man-made hazards, but six of this project's ten hazard tags are conflict tags and they are most of the hazard reporting in a Sudan dashboard. Filing them as uncategorised would label the largest group in the data as leftovers.

categories.label: Food insecurity and famine
categories.definition: NOT an IFRC codebook category. The codebook has no food-security hazard, and in Sudan famine is a consequence of conflict rather than a hazard in its own right - but food insecurity is central to this dashboard and needs to stay visible as its own thing.

categories.label: Uncategorised
categories.definition: Where a HIP code Montandon sends that this file does not hold ends up. Never guessed at; always visible. A row here is a prompt to extend hip_codes.

EN0205.note: Wildfire. UNDRR slug nat-cli-wil-wil says climatological; the IFRC codebook names Wildfires under non-technological and man-made. The codebook wins.

MH0103.note: Thunderstorm / lightning. Montandon keywords: Thunderstorm, Lightning (electrical storm), Convective-Related. Shares the nat-met-sto-sto slug with MH0301, which is why this table is keyed on the HIP code.

MH0301.note: Violent wind (GLIDE VW). Montandon keywords: Wind & Pressure-related, Dust Storm or Sandstorm. Seen as IDMC-IDU displacement events in CAR.

MH0501.note: Extreme heat. UNDRR slug nat-met-ext-hea says meteorological; the IFRC codebook files heat waves as climatological. The codebook wins.
